charter:
# Charter — T11 metrics, metering and maturity (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

- **Project:** T11 'Metrics, metering and maturity', project `01a1d039-0d36-782b-8b18-ff07a64dedbe`, track v2, project type it, ADM phase G, plateau capability, tranche 1. Issues #84 (T11) and #458 (console Metering screen) are closed; the coverage row is built at 8/8 actions, 3/3 modules and 2/2 tables, and the project row is closed with expected outputs project-brief and evidence and closure output closure-review.
- **Mandate:** make the conveyor's own process measurable from its own rows: flow, quality, cost and governance figures computed at read time; spend rolled up at tenant, department, programme, project and job and drilled down to run, step and call; C0–C5 maturity decided by versioned threshold configuration rather than opinion; and the derived cost reconciled with `billing_service` exactly at six decimals or by an incident.
- **Scope:** SPEC_V2 §7.5, §10.4 and §12; migration `0059_metrics.sql`; `crates/domain/src/metrics.rs`, `crates/store/src/metrics.rs` and `crates/actions/src/metrics/mod.rs`; the eight metrics actions; the console Metering screen reading `measure.inference` (#458). Out of scope: charging, eval- and benchmark-backed quality metrics owned by S17–S20, knowledge metrics whose ledgers do not exist (T8), and per-tool health and retirement.
- **Date:** this charter is retrospective and was authored on 2026-11-26. It records work delivered on 2026-11-19 (#84) and 2026-11-20 (#458) and the governance reconstituted on 2026-11-21; it does not attest contemporaneous intent and does not claim a live measurement after the 2026-11-21T18:50:29Z snapshot.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — T11 metrics, metering and maturity (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

body.assignment: Rework the V2 slice T11 by the reconstituted TOGAF/MSP lifecycle: author the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts, this Statement of Architecture Work, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable and the Phase-G review, and re-publish the project-brief and evidence outputs over the delivered metrics capability. The record is retrospective and dated 2026-11-26; it describes the metric families, the eight metering levels and drill-down, the C0–C5 threshold configuration, the billing reconciliation and the console Metering screen that were delivered on 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20.
body.scope: In scope: SPEC_V2 §7.5 (the metric families, the cost derivation, the metering levels and the reconciliation), §10.4 (the metrics action family) and §12 (the T11 row and its gate); migration 0059_metrics.sql with metric_threshold and metric_reconciliation; the pure rules, read models and eight actions in the Rust workspace; the eight integration tests and the tenant-isolation test; the incident card type; the served-spec lock; and the console Metering screen's live reading of measure.inference. Out of scope: charging, which remains with billing_service; the eval- and benchmark-backed quality metrics that S17–S20 own; knowledge metrics whose ledgers do not exist; and per-tool health and retirement.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect authors the pack under the standing #526 rework delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. The Architecture Board reviews and approves the seven A–D artefacts and the delivery contract, and conveyor-approver records the Phase-G level. The programme owner decides the tranche-1 exit. The pack states that the original charter, statement, contract, Phase-G review and closure review were never authored before the project closed; the rework produces them and marks them retrospective rather than reconstructing intent.
body.acceptance_criteria: The SPEC_V2 §12 gate is the contract: every metric and every metering level recomputes from rows; the reconciliation with billing_service is exact or opens an incident; a C0–C5 level changes only when the measured evidence crosses its recorded threshold; a gate that never refused is flagged. The executable form is acceptance/programme/T11.toml run by scripts/verify-project.py against the published snapshot, together with the eight metrics integration tests, the tenant-isolation test and the console checks 9b–9d. The rework records the level compliant that the Phase-G review 01a1ff90-4e19-7bcf-acbf-3f29d980572e carries against the delivery contract.
body.contract: This statement 01a1ff8d-a0ad-7a91-b026-d9a2575daa3f sits under its approval 01a1ff8d-b4cd-74f9-9f32-2b9f6cae33cd. It is complemented by the delivery contract 01a1ff8f-08ee-7bc5-bb39-81304d03c4ef on the approved scope baseline 01a1ff8f-47cb-78cf-9db8-d98d863e7dd0 (kind scope, taken 2026-11-21), and by the Phase-G review 01a1ff90-4e19-7bcf-acbf-3f29d980572e at level compliant. The statement is retrospective, dated 2026-11-26, and claims no contemporaneous sign-off.

# Stakeholder map — metrics, metering and maturity

## Metadata

Retrospective matrix for T11, authored 2026-11-26 from the 2026-11-21 rework transcript and SPEC_V2 §7.5, §10.4 and §12. Phase a, plateau psa, kind matrix; owner the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation; reviewer the Architecture Board; subject the project 01a1d039-0d36-782b-8b18-ff07a64dedbe on the v2 track, ADM phase G, tranche 1.

## Entries

Nine actors on the influence, interest and engagement axes. The programme owner decides the tranche-1 exit; the Architecture Board approves the A–D artefacts and the delivery contract; the programme manager and PMO read gate health, never-refused flags and benefit status; the BCM reads benefit realisation and the benefits a dependency slip puts at risk. Job and department owners read spend at their own level, the three tenants read tenant-scoped thresholds and spend, and the billing_service owner holds the other side of the six-decimal reconciliation. Console users read the live snapshot aggregates, and delivery teams T12 and S17–S20 consume the read models and add the eval- and benchmark-backed quality metrics.

## Links

This artefact carries one typed edge: Requirements catalog — metrics, metering and maturity as dependency, because the requirements fix what each actor receives from the figures. Every edge names another artefact this pack creates, so the set has no orphan.

## Document

Purpose: place the actors of the measurement so each concern has a named owner and a stated engagement. Scope: the project, its tranche-1 governance, the levels it meters, the tenants, the billing counterpart and the console. It was reconstructed retrospectively on 2026-11-26 from the recorded roles rather than from a live elicitation, and it does not claim that any actor re-accepted the figures after the 2026-11-21T18:50:29Z snapshot.

# Requirements catalog — metrics, metering and maturity

Retrospective catalogue for T11, authored 2026-11-26 from the 2026-11-21 rework transcript and SPEC_V2 §7.5, §10.4 and §12. Phase a, plateau psa, kind catalog; owner the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation; reviewer the Architecture Board; subject project 01a1d039-0d36-782b-8b18-ff07a64dedbe.

R11 pins the eight actions as one served surface, and R12 keeps the console on the live snapshot with no fixture fallback. # Technology standards — metrics, metering and maturity

## Metadata

Retrospective catalogue for T11, authored 2026-11-26 from the 2026-11-21 rework transcript and the delivered code. Phase d, plateau hld, kind catalog; owner the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation; reviewer the Architecture Board; subject project 01a1d039-0d36-782b-8b18-ff07a64dedbe.

## Entries

Twelve standards. PostgreSQL 18 with forced row-level security holds both T11 tables; migrations are forward-only and numbered; the Rust workspace is edition 2024 with unsafe code forbidden, and the dependency direction runs from api through actions and store to domain. One ActionSpec declaration projects to HTTP, MCP and OpenAPI, and the served-spec lock pins the eight metrics actions. Measurement is derived at read time, with no stored metric and no stored cost; money is numeric(18,6) compared at six decimals; thresholds are versioned tenant rows over a closed nine-name vocabulary. Errors use stable problem slugs, cache classes follow V1 decision D23, routes are unversioned, and the console reads only the published snapshot.

## Links

This artefact carries one typed edge: Data entity catalog — metrics, metering and maturity as derivation, because each entity is held in one of these formats. Every edge names another artefact this pack creates, so the set has no orphan.

## Document

Purpose: name the formats, disciplines and instruments T11 fixes for measurement, precision, configuration and the console. Scope: store, migrations, the action surface, precision, error slugs and the snapshot-only console rule. It was authored retrospectively on 2026-11-26 and names only standards that the delivered migration, code and tests actually apply.

# Architecture Artefact Index — T11 (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Metadata

The artefact set for T11 is the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts on the delivery track: the stakeholder map, the driver/goal/objective catalogue, the requirements catalogue and the solution concept at phase a, plateau psa, and the business capability map, the data entity catalogue and the technology standards at phases b, c and d, plateau hld. Each is an approved row with a published body dated 2026-11-22; the owner is the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation, the reviewer is the Architecture Board, and the subject is project 01a1d039-0d36-782b-8b18-ff07a64dedbe.

## Entries

The set is seven rows in the order the standard seeds them: Stakeholder map — metrics, metering and maturity (matrix), Driver/goal/objective — metrics, metering and maturity (catalog), Requirements catalog — metrics, metering and maturity (catalog), Solution concept — metrics, metering and maturity (diagram), Business capability map — metrics, metering and maturity (diagram), Data entity catalog — metrics, metering and maturity (catalog) and Technology standards — metrics, metering and maturity (catalog). They carry nine stakeholders, seven drivers, twelve requirements, seventeen components and edges, twelve capabilities, thirteen entities and twelve standards.

## Links

The typed edges are: the driver catalogue derives from the stakeholder map; the requirements catalogue derives from the driver catalogue; the solution concept realizes the requirements catalogue; the capability map derives from the solution concept and the requirements catalogue; the data entity catalogue derives from the capability map and the solution concept; and the technology standards derive from the data entity catalogue. Every edge names another artefact of this pack, so no artefact is an orphan.

## Document

The index is the architecture-artifact page the artefact standard reads. The seven artefact documents were published on 2026-11-22 as approved instances after the 2026-11-21 rework; this index is the retrospective page authored on 2026-11-26 over them, and it names no document row that the snapshot does not hold.

risk.title: A metrics read that starts writing a roll-up row would turn derived figures into a second store
risk.body: The whole design rests on reading the ledgers at request time: metrics.flow, metrics.job, metrics.usage, metrics.programme and metrics.maturity are aggregates, and migration 0059_metrics.sql adds only metric_threshold and metric_reconciliation. A later change that writes a roll-up or cost row would create a second source that can drift from the ledger it summarises. This retrospective row, recorded 2026-11-26, keeps the invariant visible and ties it to the migration and the tests that prove it today.

meta.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

risk.title: A stale billing total could match the derived cost by accident
risk.body: metrics.reconcile compares the derived cost with the total that billing.summary attests for the period. A difference opens an incident, but an unreachable service is recorded as unavailable and an old attested total could in principle coincide with the derived figure. The reconciliation rule reduces the exposure to a coincidence across both figures and the period; this row records it on 2026-11-26 so the incident path is not treated as a licence to ignore the period.

meta.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

risk.title: A tenant with few approvals can reach C1 on a very small sample
risk.body: The C0–C5 ladder moves only when the recorded evidence crosses the configured minimum, and the nine-name vocabulary includes approvals.decided and approvals.approval_rate. A tenant with five decided approvals can meet a rate threshold on a sample too small to mean much. The mechanism is honest about the numbers it reads and the level names its threshold version; this row records the calibration risk on 2026-11-26 rather than asserting that every tenant's first threshold row is statistically comfortable.

meta.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

issue.title: The original T11 governance record was never authored
issue.body: T11 closed without a charter, Statement of Architecture Work, delivery contract, Phase-G review, closure review or published output, and with all seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts absent. The contemporaneous evidence is the merged code, the coverage row, the served-spec lock and the git history. This issue records the gap on 2026-11-26 and points to the retrospective pack that closes it; it does not pretend the record existed before the rework.

issue.title: Eval- and benchmark-backed quality metrics sit outside T11
issue.body: SPEC_V2 §7.5 names first-pass yield, rework rate, defect escapes, eval score and benchmark delta as quality metrics, but their ledgers are owned by S17–S20. T11 delivers the approval- and run-derived quality figures only, and says so. This issue keeps the boundary explicit on 2026-11-26 so a reader of the T11 quality family does not read an absent eval figure as a zero.

assumption.title: billing.summary's attested total is the charging system's authoritative figure for the period
assumption.body: The reconciliation compares the conveyor's derived cost with the total that billing.summary declares. The assumption is that the declared total is the charging system's own figure for the same tenant and period, not a cached or adjusted copy, because a difference is raised as an incident rather than absorbed. This retrospective row records the assumption on 2026-11-26; if the declared total is not authoritative, the incident would compare against the wrong number and the reconciliation would be formally exact and substantively wrong.

assumption.title: The published snapshot's measure.inference window is representative enough to display
assumption.body: The console Metering screen renders the snapshot's measure.inference totals at 2026-11-21T18:50:29Z: 609 calls, 9,458,468 tokens, 606 cache misses, 0 hits, 3 unknown cache classes and 0 non-ok calls. That is the whole ledger at one instant, not a bounded business period. The assumption is that an all-time figure is honest for a console that labels it as the snapshot's own aggregate; a windowed figure is an API parameter, not a stored roll-up. Recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-26.

dependency.title: Every T11 figure depends on the ledgers it reads
dependency.body: The metric families recompute from inference_call and tool_call for spend, run and run_step for attribution, approval for governance, card, list and event for flow, the organisation join for department attribution, the benefit rows for realisation and commercial_price for the derived cost. If a ledger stops being written, the corresponding figure becomes unavailable or empty rather than wrong; the dependency is on the rows existing at read time. This retrospective row records the dependency on 2026-11-26.

dependency.title: The console depends on the published snapshot, not on a live metrics call
dependency.body: The Metering screen reads measure.inference from the published snapshot and renders the snapshot's own cost note; when the section is absent it says the measurement is not published rather than borrowing a fixture. The dependency runs from the console to the snapshot generator, so a snapshot published without the section is visible as an honest absence instead of a stale number. This row records the dependency on 2026-11-26 and ties it to issue #458 and the console checks 9b–9d.

benefit.title: Every metric is computed from rows, so a figure cannot drift from the ledger it summarises
benefit.body: The five read actions are aggregates over the conveyor's own rows and migration 0059 creates no metric table. The benefit is that a reported flow, quality, cost or governance figure has no second store to fall out of step with the ledger, and a new ledger row changes the figure on the next read. This retrospective row links the benefit to the read-time design on 2026-11-26.

benefit.title: Billing divergence surfaces as an incident rather than a silent adjustment
benefit.body: metrics.reconcile compares the derived cost with the declared billing.summary total at six decimals; a difference opens an incident carrying both figures, and an unreachable service is unavailable rather than zero. The benefit is that the money question has a named owner and a record instead of an adjustment made after the fact. This retrospective row links the benefit to the reconciliation rule on 2026-11-26.

# Project brief — T11 metrics, metering and maturity (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Outcome

Every flow, quality, cost and governance figure the conveyor reports is a read-time computation over its own rows; spend rolls up at tenant, department, programme, project, job, run, step and call; C0–C5 maturity is decided by versioned threshold configuration; and the derived cost reconciles with billing_service exactly at six decimals or opens an incident. The console Metering screen reads the published snapshot's measure.inference aggregates and shows no fixture number when the section is absent.

## Boundary

Out of scope: charging, which remains with billing_service; the eval- and benchmark-backed quality metrics — first-pass yield, rework rate, defect escapes, eval score and benchmark delta — whose ledgers S17–S20 own; knowledge metrics whose ledgers do not exist (T8); and per-tool health and retirement. T11 must not fork a stored metric or a stored cost: a metrics read writes no metric row, the migration adds only metric_threshold and metric_reconciliation, and the console never recomputes cost from a stale cache.

## Reuse sources
The measurement reads the conveyor's existing ledgers rather than a new store: inference_call and tool_call for tokens and spend; run and run_step for attribution and drill-down; approval for governance; card, list and event for flow; job_binding, job_department and department for organisation attribution; benefit_profile, benefit_transition, benefit_link and project_dependency for MSP metrics; and commercial_price for the derived cost. It adds only the versioned threshold configuration, the reconciliation verdict, the eight actions and the console unit.

## Inception units

T11 is the measurement slice and has no separate inception analysis or architecture spike: its inputs are the metric definitions in SPEC_V2 §7.5 and the ledgers named above. The retrospective reconstitutes the governance record over the completed work — charter, Statement of Architecture Work, the seven A–D artefacts approved by the board, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable, the Phase-G review, this brief, the evidence page and the closure review — against the 2026-11-21 rework and the 2026-11-22 artefact publications.

## Dependencies

The project row records depends_on as needs P0, the programme definition. It is related to S02 and T1, the other tranche-1 projects, and it blocks T12, which follows all V2 slices. Operationally every figure depends on its ledger being written: a missing ledger is reported as unavailable with a reason, never as zero. The reconciliation depends on billing.summary's attested total, and the console depends on the published snapshot carrying measure.inference. In governance the pack rests on the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14, the approved scope baseline 01a1ff8f-47cb-78cf-9db8-d98d863e7dd0 and the delivery contract 01a1ff8f-08ee-7bc5-bb39-81304d03c4ef.

## Acceptance

The SPEC_V2 §12 gate is the contract: every metric and every metering level recomputes from rows; the reconciliation with billing_service is exact or opens an incident; a C0–C5 level changes only when the measured evidence crosses its recorded threshold; a gate that never refused is flagged. The executable form is acceptance/programme/T11.toml run by scripts/verify-project.py against the published snapshot, backed by the eight metrics integration tests, metric_thresholds_are_tenant_isolated and the console checks 9b–9d. The Phase-G review 01a1ff90-4e19-7bcf-acbf-3f29d980572e records the level compliant.

## Capabilities

The eight metrics actions — metrics.flow, metrics.job, metrics.usage, metrics.programme, metrics.maturity, metrics.reconcile, metrics.threshold_get and metrics.threshold_update — deliver the five metric families, the eight metering levels and the run, step and call drill-down, the contiguous C0–C5 ladder over versioned thresholds, the six-decimal billing reconciliation with an incident on divergence, and the console Metering screen over the snapshot's live inference aggregates. The two T11 tables are tenant-isolated, and the nine-name evidence vocabulary is closed.

## Plan

The plan is docs/SPEC_V2.md §12 (T11) against §7.5 and §10.4. The metrics capability was delivered by issue #84, merged 2026-11-19, and the console unit by issue #458, merged 2026-11-20. The governance was reconstituted and the project re-closed on 2026-11-21; the seven artefact documents were published on 2026-11-22. This brief is retrospective and dated 2026-11-26: it records that work and the record above it, and it does not claim a contemporaneous plan or a measurement later than the 2026-11-21T18:50:29Z snapshot.

# Closure review — T11 metrics, metering and maturity (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Outcome vs acceptance

The outcome the charter records is a conveyor whose own process is measurable from its own rows, and the acceptance the record carries matches it clause by clause: every metric and every metering level recomputes from rows with no metric table; the reconciliation with billing_service matches at six decimals or opens an incident; a C0–C5 level moves only across recorded threshold versions and stops at the first unmet level; and a gate with decided approvals and no rejections is flagged. The evidence is the eight metrics integration tests, metric_thresholds_are_tenant_isolated, the console checks 9b–9d and the green acceptance/programme/T11.toml manifest. The Phase-G review 01a1ff90-4e19-7bcf-acbf-3f29d980572e records the level compliant against the delivery contract 01a1ff8f-08ee-7bc5-bb39-81304d03c4ef.

## Evidence

The evidence is migration 0059_metrics.sql with metric_threshold and metric_reconciliation, the pure rules in crates/domain/src/metrics.rs, the read models in crates/store/src/metrics.rs, the eight actions in crates/actions/src/metrics/mod.rs, the eight integration tests, the tenant-isolation test and served-spec.lock.json. The console evidence is docs/design/v2.js meteringLive(), check-v2.cjs 9b–9d and the snapshot's measure.json at 2026-11-21T18:50:29Z, which reports 609 calls, 9,458,468 tokens, 606 misses, 0 hits, 3 unknown cache classes and 0 non-ok calls. The governance record is the Statement of Architecture Work 01a1ff8d-a0ad-7a91-b026-d9a2575daa3f, the delivery contract 01a1ff8f-08ee-7bc5-bb39-81304d03c4ef, the scope baseline 01a1ff8f-47cb-78cf-9db8-d98d863e7dd0 and the rework note with its 39 recorded acts.

## Open items

One item is structural and not closable by this pack: the original charter, Statement of Architecture Work, delivery contract, Phase-G review and closure review were never authored, so the contemporaneous record is the merged code, the coverage row, the action lock and the git history, and this set is retrospective. ## Decision

The retrospective decision is to close on the record the snapshot carries, at the level compliant that the Phase-G review 01a1ff90-4e19-7bcf-acbf-3f29d980572e records, with the residuals stated rather than waived. The decision is dated 2026-11-26 and rests on the approved contract, the approved baseline, the seven A–D artefacts and the test evidence; it does not assert a contemporaneous review that was never written and does not reopen the classification of any metric family that belongs to another slice.
